meta.titre: The Japanese Invasion of Manchuria: why Japan struck in 1931 and why the League failed to stop it
meta.sous_theme: Causes, course and consequences of the Manchurian crisis, 1931 to 1933

sections.contenu_markdown: In 1931 an explosion damaged a railway line in north-east China, and within months a large region was in the hands of the Japanese army. The Manchurian crisis was the first big test of the League of Nations after the First World War, and the League failed it. For O Level students the event matters because it shows how aggression was allowed to succeed in the 1930s. Examiners ask both why Japan attacked and why the League did nothing effective. This course gives you the facts and a method to answer.

items: The League of Nations was an international organisation created after the First World War to keep peace.
Raw materials, such as coal and iron, are needed by factories.
A puppet state is a state that looks independent but is controlled by another country.

sections.titre: Manchuria: why Japan attacked and what followed
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Background

Manchuria is a region in north-east China, rich in coal and iron ore. Since the early twentieth century Japan held railway rights and mines in the south of Manchuria, and a Japanese army, the Kwantung Army, guarded the South Manchurian Railway.

### Why Japan attacked in 1931

| Cause | Explanation |
|---|---|
| Raw materials and markets | Japan is a crowded island country with few resources; Manchuria offered coal, iron and a market |
| Great Depression | After 1929 world trade collapsed, Japanese exports such as silk fell and many people suffered, so conquest seemed a remedy |
| Power of the army | Military leaders and nationalists gained influence over the weak civilian government and wanted an empire |
| Weak China | China was divided and busy with civil strife, so it could not resist well |
| Weak world reaction | Great powers were busy with the Depression, and the League had no army |

### Course

1. In September 1931 an explosion damaged the railway near Mukden. Japanese officers blamed Chinese soldiers; historians generally believe that the officers had arranged it as an excuse.
2. The Kwantung Army occupied Manchuria within a few months.
3. In 1932 Japan set up a puppet state called Manchukuo, with Puyi, the last Chinese emperor, as its head.

### The League's response

China appealed to the League, which sent the Lytton Commission. The Commission reported that Japan had acted wrongly in taking Manchuria, and the League accepted its report. Japan then announced its withdrawal from the League in 1933. The League had no army, Britain and France were unwilling to fight in distant Asia, and the United States was not a member.

### Results

The League was shown to be weak. Japan moved on to a full-scale war with China in 1937, and other aggressors, such as Italy, took note.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks why Japan attacked
variantes.contenu_markdown: Give three to four causes as economic, political and military. For each cause, state the fact and then explain how it led Japan to attack. Always mention the Great Depression, because it ties the economic and the political causes together.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the command word is State, Name or Give the year
variantes.contenu_markdown: Learn a short list: Manchuria, 1931, Mukden, Kwantung Army, Manchukuo, Puyi, Lytton Commission, 1933. Write the fact asked for and stop.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks why the League did not stop Japan
variantes.contenu_markdown: Link each cause of failure to the League itself: no army, dependence on the great powers, unwillingness of Britain and France to act in Asia, absence of the United States, slow methods such as sending a commission that took many months.

sections.enonce_markdown: Explain how the Mukden Incident helped Japan to take over Manchuria. [6 marks]

etapes.action: Identify the command word and the central term.
etapes.justification: 'Explain how' asks for a process: what happened and why it helped Japan.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Aim: show how an event became an excuse for conquest.

etapes.justification: The facts are the evidence you will build on.
etapes.resultat_markdown: In September 1931 an explosion damaged the Japanese-owned railway near Mukden.

etapes.action: State what the Japanese army did.
etapes.justification: This links the incident to the takeover.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The Kwantung Army blamed China, used the explosion as an excuse and occupied Mukden and then the rest of Manchuria.

etapes.justification: A good explanation gives the reasons that made the plan succeed.
etapes.resultat_markdown: China was weak, and the League and the great powers were slow to react.

etapes.justification: A conclusion rounds off the explanation.
etapes.resultat_markdown: In 1932 Japan set up Manchukuo as a puppet state.

sections.conclusion_markdown: Model answer: The Mukden Incident gave Japan an excuse to take Manchuria. In September 1931 an explosion damaged the Japanese-owned railway near Mukden. Japanese army officers blamed Chinese soldiers and used this to justify military action, although historians generally believe that the officers had arranged the explosion themselves. The Kwantung Army occupied Mukden and then the rest of Manchuria within a few months. The plan worked because China was weak and divided, and because the League of Nations and the great powers were slow to react. In 1932 Japan set up a puppet state called Manchukuo. In this way a small incident was turned into the conquest of a whole region.

items.pourquoi_faux: The invasion was in 1931. The year 1941 is linked with Japan's attack on Pearl Harbor.
items.correction_markdown: Write 1931 for the invasion of Manchuria and 1937 for the full war with China.

items.erreur_markdown: Manchuria was a part of Korea or of Japan.
items.pourquoi_faux: Manchuria was a region of north-east China, and Japan took it by force.
items.correction_markdown: Write that Japan attacked and occupied the Chinese region of Manchuria.

items.erreur_markdown: The League of Nations sent an army to throw out the Japanese.
items.pourquoi_faux: The League had no army and relied on its members. It sent a commission and made a report.
items.correction_markdown: Write that the League investigated, condemned Japan in its report and then could not enforce its decision.

items.erreur_markdown: Japan attacked only because of the Great Depression.
items.pourquoi_faux: The Depression was important, but army power, resources and the weakness of China also mattered.
items.correction_markdown: Give several causes and, if the question asks, say which was most important and why.

items.enonce_markdown: Where is Manchuria, and why was it valuable to Japan?
items.solution_markdown: Manchuria is a region in north-east China. It was valuable because it had coal and iron ore, a market for Japanese goods and railway interests that Japan already held. **A region in north-east China, rich in raw materials.**

items.enonce_markdown: Explain why the League of Nations failed to stop Japan in Manchuria.
items.solution_markdown: Award marks for: the League had no army and relied on its members; Britain and France were unwilling to fight a distant war during the Depression; the United States was not a member; the League sent a commission whose report took a long time; Japan simply left the League in 1933. **The League could condemn Japan but could not enforce its decision.**

items.enonce_markdown: Assess the importance of the Great Depression compared with other causes of the Japanese attack on Manchuria. [8 marks]
items.solution_markdown: Award marks for the Depression: collapse of exports such as silk, hardship in Japan and the argument that empire would provide markets and raw materials. Award marks for other causes: army and nationalist influence, existing railway rights, weak China, weak reaction by the League. Credit a reasoned judgement, for example: **the Depression created the pressure, but the power of the army made the attack possible.**

items_markdown: Manchuria is a region of north-east China with coal and iron ore, where Japan held railway rights.
Causes of the 1931 attack: resources and markets, the Great Depression, power of the army, a weak China and a weak world reaction.
Course: Mukden Incident in September 1931, occupation of Manchuria, puppet state of Manchukuo in 1932.
The Lytton Commission criticised Japan's action, and Japan announced its withdrawal from the League in 1933.
The League failed because it had no army and its main members were unwilling to act.
The crisis showed that aggression could succeed and encouraged other aggressors.
